decisive_items: TSC1 gene mutation (15 exon c.1690 G > T, p.E564*)
subcortical tubers in white matter of frontal lobes
response.rationale: The constellation of TSC1 mutation, cardiac rhabdomyoma, hypopigmented macules, and cortical tubers is diagnostic of Tuberous Sclerosis Complex. The posterior fossa mass is a manifestation of TSC, not a separate primary diagnosis.

rejected.why: Cardiac rhabdomyoma is a feature of TSC, not the overall diagnosis.
Histopathology shows epithelioid cells with EMA/S100/pan-CK/brachyury, not typical rhabdoid morphology; no INI1/SMARCB1 loss mentioned.
Depigmented spots are hypopigmented macules, not melanocytic nevi or hyperpigmentation; no leptomeningeal melanosis.
SEGA is a TSC-associated tumor but typically periventricular; the posterior fossa mass with brainstem compression is not characteristic, and TSC is the underlying syndrome.
